subject: Drop down menu/select box and shiny

messages.author: 5ffb80c386af5188
messages.subject: Drop down menu/select box and shiny
parts:
I'm having problem with a drop down menu/select box and ggivs in shiny. This is an approximation using the 'cocaine' data set. 

I'm trying to use the drop down to filter which x and y values to plot (here, ~potency and ~weight, based on the state). I know where the code is failing, I just have no idea what it should look like. 

# ui.R
library(shiny)


shinyUI(fluidPage(
  titlePanel("Seizures by State"),
 
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
     
 uiOutput("choose_state")
    ),
   
    mainPanel(
    ggvisOutput("ggvis")    
    )
  )
))



# server.R

library(ggvis)
library(dplyr)

state_names <- sort(unique(cocaine$state))

 shinyServer(function(input, output) {
 
 output$choose_state <- renderUI({
 
 # Create drop down and populate with 'state_names'
    selectInput("state", "Choose State", state_names)
 })

 #create vis
 cocaine %>% ggvis(~potency, ~weight) %>% filter(state == eval(state_names, selected = "AK")) %>% layer_points(fill := "dodgerblue")  %>% bind_shiny("ggvis")

})



I know the expression inside the eval parenthesis is wrong. Now, I also know I can do the following line in the server script instead and get something that works, even if it does have redundant drop downs. 

 cocaine %>% ggvis(~potency, ~weight) %>% filter(state == eval(input_select(state_names, selected = "AK"))) %>% layer_points(fill := "dodgerblue")  %>% bind_shiny("ggvis", "ggvis_ui")



It's pretty cool that ggvis can essentially generate its own widgets. The obvious question then is, 'Why don't you just do it that way and get rid of the sidebar widget?'

Well, the actual project I'm working on has three drop downs with dependencies. In other words, the second drop down is populated based on the value in the first pull down, and the third is populated based on the value in the second drop down (it's someone else's proprietary data so I can't use it here).

What I need is the value coming out of that final drop down as the filter value. It would be the equivalent of the 'state' (or 'input$state') from the sidebar pull down ('selectInput') in the first bit of server code above. I need that value to be the filter for the x and y values. 

So I can't use one created from within the ggvis code. 

I've tried just about everything I can think of (creating additional variables, making a function that passes off the variable, reactive expressions). They all end in various errors. This should be straightforward, no? 

Any help is appreciated.

parts:
I guess I'm not clear on how this is a dplyr problem

Just walking through this, I know what I need to get is essentially:

blah blah %>% filter(state, 'by the value that gets returned as input$state from the input_select widget') %>% etc

Now I know I can't just drop 'input$state' into the line as I can only access 'input$state' if it's inside a reactive expression. And I've tried every manner of reactive expression, that I can think of. 

If I do something like:

stateVar <- reactiveText({
 tempVar <- input$state

 return(tempVar)
})


I can't drop stateVar into my ggvis line because it's a function. And if I try to turn the function into a variable, like:

 thisVar <- tempVar()

and drop that in the filter command, I get a warning telling me I'm trying to do something that I can only do from within a reactive expression. I spend most of yesterday trying to wrestle with this and I'm kinda stuck.

If I've done something horribly stupid, the easy answer to "Why would you do that?" is: "I'm not a coder." At some level that's not really a good excuse. Especially when I'm this deep into a package that's still in development but I mostly do stats and I mostly work in R; all the languages I've had to use, I've had to teach myself to get some task accomplished so while I'm slowly accumulating more skills, I don't have a good formal background and often make rookie mistake. In this instance I was able to originally get the job done using the base graphics, but now I need to be able to get some info in the output into some tooltips, and the tooltips that work with the base graphics are inadequate for what we're trying to achieve. 

Usually I'm finding examples of things that work and altering or reverse engineering to fit my needs. I'm not looking for someone to just hand me answers. How else am I going to learn if I don't figure some things out for myself. But every now and then I just hit a point where I'm stuck and can't find the right resource to get me over the hurdle.

I think you can simplify your problem to this:

my_state <- "AK"
cocaine %>% filter(state == my_state)

In shiny, you'd make this a reactive:

cur_state <- reactive(cocaine %>% filter(state == input$state))

and then pass that to ggvis

cur_state %>%
ggvis() %>% ...


Hadley

Thanks Hadley.

Now I feel stupid. That totally makes sense. And I was attacking the problem in the wrong place. 

I recoded, but am still having a problem. Here's the code in a single R file. 


library(shiny)

library(ggvis)
library(dplyr)
state_names <- sort(unique(cocaine$state))

#options(shiny.trace=FALSE)


shinyApp(
 ui= fluidPage(

  titlePanel("Cocaine by State"),

 sidebarLayout(

    sidebarPanel(

 uiOutput("choose_state")

    ),

    mainPanel(

     ggvisOutput("ggvis")    

    )
  )
),

 server = function(input, output) {

 output$choose_state <- renderUI({

 # Create drop down and populate with 'state_names'

    selectInput("states", "Choose State", state_names)            
 })

 cur_state <- reactive({

 cocaine %>% filter(state == states)
})

 if(is.null(dim(cur_state))){

 cur_state <- cocaine[cocaine$state == "AK",]

 }

 cur_state %>% ggvis(~potency, ~weight) %>% layer_points(fill := "dodgerblue") %>% bind_shiny("ggvis")

 }
)




I originally thought it wasn't working because without a selected value to start (having a default state to plot) it would throw an error (something like: 'expecting 3380 values, getting zero'; cocaine has 3380 rows). After fumbling with the proper way to do that, I just clumsily hacked it with an 'if' statement. So it starts with 'AK'.

But once I got something plotted nothing was happening. Changing the value on the selector didn't update the chart. I dropped in a trace statement to see what was happening and no matter what 'cur_state' was coming back as NULL. 

So, is this just a syntax error somewhere on my part? Logically it makes sense. The reactive expression is returning a data.frame (correct?) and that df is then the basis of my ggvis statement. Why is it returning a NULL value?

I recoded, but am still having a problem. Here's the code in a single R file. 


library(shiny)
library(ggvis)
library(dplyr)
state_names <- sort(unique(cocaine$state))

#options(shiny.trace=FALSE)


shinyApp(
 ui= fluidPage(

  titlePanel("Cocaine by State"),

 sidebarLayout(

    sidebarPanel(

 uiOutput("choose_state")

    ),

    mainPanel(

     ggvisOutput("ggvis")    

    )
  )
),

 output$choose_state <- renderUI({

 # Create drop down and populate with 'state_names'

    selectInput("states", "Choose State", state_names)            
 })

 cur_state <- reactive({

 cocaine %>% filter(state == states)
})

 if(is.null(dim(cur_state))){

 cur_state <- cocaine[cocaine$state == "AK",]

 }

 cur_state %>% ggvis(~potency, ~weight) %>% layer_points(fill := "dodgerblue") %>% bind_shiny("ggvis")

 }

But once I got something plotted nothing was happening. Changing the value on the selector didn't update the chart. I dropped in a trace statement to see what was happening and no matter what 'cur_state' was coming back as NULL. 

So, is this just a syntax error somewhere on my part? Logically it makes sense. The reactive expression is returning a data.frame (correct?) and that df is then the basis of my ggvis statement. Why is it returning a NULL value?

So I spent some more time playing with this. And I'm starting to think there is something wrong with using 'filter' inside a reactive expression with shiny. 

Basically I took the exact same code from above and just changed from using 'filter' to using 'slice'. I changed almost nothing else* and now I get a working graph that updates with a change in the pull down. 

* I say 'nothing' but I made a really poor attempt to have the pulldown give two ranges (1:1690 and 1691:3380) but all it did was populate the pulldown with single numbers (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, etc...) but really that's not too important. So I only slice the data.frame by 1 row at a time. As long as you keep the axes fixed (that's the other stuff I added) you get watch the one dot move every time you change the pull down.
